goal: Pat (drawn young, about five years old) lifts one corner of the big paper map on the wall of the same book corner and looks at the empty wall behind it. No letters, words, or numbers anywhere.
colorPrompt: Compose one children's book picture from the element pictures. Picture 1 shows the boy Pat: the four 3D views at the bottom are the approved character, and the flat drawing at the top is only a hint, so copy the 3D look; ignore the gray background, the labels, and the shadow; the teddy bear in his arms is not part of this picture, so leave the bear out. Picture 2 is the empty book corner of the kindergarten classroom: cream plaster walls with dark-brown timber beams, a light wooden floor, ONE big round wicker basket full of colorful picture books at the left, ONE big cream paper map with a blue river, a green hill, and a small red house on the wall, and ONE wooden toy kitchen at the right with a small RED toy pan on its cooker; use it as the background and keep the same corner. Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The children keep their chibi proportions: a big head and a small body. Hands are small, clean hands with five clear short fingers (four fingers and one thumb) when open, never fists unless stated, and a hanging hand shows relaxed, separate short fingers. Rendering errors to NOT copy from the character pictures: a tiny dark tick mark or pale skin flap at the outer corner of an eye, and a faint pale crease on a forehead. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner; no character here has an eyelash flick. Clean eye corners, no streak on the forehead, no marks on the face. The ears are smooth, with one clean rounded rim. Each piece of clothing is one even color with no pale patches, no pale blotches at the shoulders, and no stains. Do not change anyone's skin tone, hair, or clothes. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing on any picture or sign. The picture is for young children and is rated G. Keep each character exactly as in the pictures: Pat: a five-year-old boy with a chibi look (a big head and a small body), short messy black hair with a fringe and a few small tufts on top, big brown eyes, a green T-shirt, brown cargo shorts, brown sandals; he holds no teddy bear and carries no bag. The picture: Pat lifts one corner of the big paper map and looks at the empty wall behind it. A medium-wide shot at a low camera height in the book corner (picture 2), the whole bodies of the children in view; the basket, the map, and the toy kitchen with its red pan stay as in picture 2. The big paper map hangs a little lower on the wall than in picture 2, so that Pat can reach its lower right corner. Pat stands on the floor in front of the wall in the middle of the picture, turned about three quarters toward the wall, reaches up with one hand, and lifts the lower right corner of the map. Behind the lifted corner the wall is plain empty cream plaster: no hole, no door, no picture, and nothing hidden. Pat looks at the empty wall with raised eyebrows and a curious face. No mats and no puppy. Exactly one boy and one map. Exactly the characters named here are in the picture, and no other person or animal. A character of the pictures that this description does not name must not appear. Every named character has a clear, whole, friendly face. The page text is "Pat can see a map." and is context only: do not draw any text.
linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: thick, even black lines (about three times a normal outline), simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw the mouth exactly as in picture 1: an open mouth stays an open mouth drawn as a closed outline, and a closed smile stays one curve. Draw each hand as a closed outline with each finger as a separate rounded shape. Each head of hair is one closed shape. The ear is one closed outline with at most one inner curve. No lines on the clothes other than the outline, the collar, the cuffs, the buttons, the straps, the stripes, and the pocket. No wrinkle lines on any face. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes (the floor line, the wall lines, each timber beam as one closed band, the basket as one closed shape with its books as a few big closed rectangles, the map as one closed rectangle with its river, its hill, and its house as closed shapes, the toy kitchen as one closed box shape with its shelf and its oven door as closed shapes, the red pan as one closed shape with one closed handle, and each mat as one closed rounded rectangle). No wood grain lines, no floor plank lines, no basket weave lines, no wall texture, no hatching, no tick marks, no small details. Every outline is one closed line that never runs into a background line; no loose line ends anywhere. Every line inside an object ends on another line. Use few background shapes. Pat's hair is one closed shape; his shirt, each cargo-shorts pocket, and each sandal are closed shapes. Each hand is one closed outline with five fingers drawn as separate rounded closed shapes (four fingers and one thumb). The map is one closed rectangle with its lifted corner as one closed curl shape; the empty wall behind the corner stays empty.
